images.title: Parity rules for sums and differences
images.purpose: Shows the rule table odd ± odd is even, even ± even is even, odd ± even is odd, applied to 543 − 479.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One 2 by 2 rule table in the centre with one example tag below it.
images.exact_structure: A table with 3 columns and 3 rows of square cells, thin dark outlines. Top left cell holds the sign ±. Top row headers: odd, even. Left column headers: odd, even. The four answer cells: odd row and odd column is even; odd row and even column is odd; even row and odd column is odd; even row and even column is even. The two even answer cells are filled light green (#009E73); the two odd answer cells are filled light amber (#E69F00). The odd and odd cell has a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline. Under the table, one line: 543 − 479: odd − odd = even, with a thin reddish purple (#CC79A7) arrow from it up to the outlined cell. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The parity of a sum or difference follows from the parities of its parts, without computing.

image_decisions.why: A single rule table lets students decide parity without computing.
